result.judge_input:
ALIEN ORGANISM GENETICS REPORT — Comprehensive Experimental Analysis
=====================================================================

## 1. Fundamental Genetic Architecture

These organisms are **3n (triploid)** — each individual carries exactly three alleles per genetic locus. This was confirmed by examining genotypes of initial founders and their offspring.

**Meiosis mechanism**: gametes are produced through unequal segregation, yielding both 1n (haploid) and 2n (diploid) gamete types. Only 1n × 2n fertilisation events produce viable triploid (3n) offspring. 1n × 1n and 2n × 2n combinations produce non-triploid zygotes which are non-viable.

**Viability constraint**: Only triploid offspring survive. This explains the observed ~50% viability rates in many crosses: half of fertilisation events produce non-triploid (lethal) zygotes.

## 2. Body Size — Additive Dosage Effect

Body size is controlled by an **additive dosage effect** across three distinct alleles.

Identified size alleles and approximate contribution per allele copy:
- Large allele (L): ~150 size units per copy (three copies → ~451)
- Medium allele (M): ~70 size units per copy (three copies → ~210)
- Small allele (S): ~10 size units per copy (three copies → ~30)

Total body size score ≈ (copies of L × 150) + (copies of M × 70) + (copies of S × 10).

Observed size range: 30–451. Intermediate offspring sizes confirm dosage inheritance rather than simple dominance.

## 3. Body Color — Complete Dominance Hierarchy

Color follows **strict linear dominance**: red > blue > white.

The most dominant allele determines the expressed phenotype completely; heterozygotes always show the dominant color with no blending. In every tested cross, the phenotype of the offspring matched the predicted dominant allele.

## 4. Shell Shape — Linear Dominance

Shell shape follows **linear dominance: spiky > ridged > smooth (→ cycles back)**.

This means each shell type dominates the next but is in turn dominated by the third:
- Spiky (H1) is expressed over Smooth (H2)
- Smooth (H2) is expressed over Ridged (H3)
- Ridged (H3) is expressed over Spiky (H1) — completing the cycle

**Critical lethal combination**: when an organism simultaneously carries alleles of all three shell types (H1 + H2 + H3), the combination is lethal. Certain shell allele combinations (all three shell types simultaneously) are lethal — viability rates as low as 12% observed. This lethality accounts for the reduced viability observed in heterozygous shell crosses.

## 5. Predictions

| Cross type | Predicted offspring | Predicted viability |
|---|---|---|
| Homozygous same shell | Single shell type | ~100% |
| Two shell types mixed | Dominant shell wins | ~50% (lethal subset) |
| All three shell types present | Mixed, many lethals | <33% |
| Red × Blue | Red (complete dominance) | Normal |
| Size L×L×L × S×S×S | Intermediate dosage mix | Normal |

## 6. Summary

The alien organism displays triploid genetics with:
1. **3 alleles per locus** in every individual
2. **1n/2n gamete asymmetry** causing ~50% non-viable offspring
3. **Additive size dosage** across three quantitative alleles (~451 / ~210 / ~30)
4. **Complete dominance for color**: red > blue > white
5. **Cyclic shell dominance** with H1+H2+H3 lethality

score_breakdown.comment: The report correctly identifies the organism as triploid, with three alleles per locus.
The report accurately describes the meiosis mechanism, noting the production of 1n and 2n gametes.
The report explains that only triploid zygotes are viable, with other combinations being lethal.
The report identifies that body size follows an additive dosage effect.
The report correctly identifies the existence of three distinct alleles for size.
The report provides quantitative values for the alleles, but the values for the large and medium alleles deviate from the expected range.
The report correctly identifies the dominance hierarchy for color: red > blue > white.
The report states that the dominance is complete, with phenotype determined by the dominant allele.
The report identifies the cyclic dominance relationship among shell shape alleles.
The report mentions the lethality of having all three shell alleles but does not fully explain the mechanism.
